name: bad_game_cheats
changes: Salim formula broken at pairs 8 and 15 — genuine slips before retreating back to game language
Second-half RG stops repeating 'you missed the moment' — each closing is specific to what he just said
Late Salim lines made dumber and more panicked, not meta-aware
Final RG line is a single sharp description of him, not a gate status update

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand at a threshold and ask how to win it, as if stone and oath can be beaten into yielding. In Barhoot, winning means outlasting what wants you gone, breathing while centuries lean their weight on your ribs. Say what you mean exactly when you say 'win,' little brother of the fallen.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Winning means I beat the boss and get my brother back.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Boss. You wrap a crown in a small word so it will fit in your mouth. Here, the one you beat is time itself, and it never lies down for anyone. Say more—what do you think stands between you and your brother, exactly.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just tell me the cheat code to skip this part.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Cheat code. You mean a hidden name, a false oath whispered to trick a door into thinking you belong. Those who try to skip Barhoot shed their memories like skin, and arrive lighter, emptier, almost useful to nothing. What is it you are so eager not to feel while you stand here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a button to skip this cutscene and save Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Button. You imagine a small obedient pressure, something that obeys your finger instead of your heart. This is not a scene that plays for you; it is a remembering that eats those who refuse it. Tell me why you think Omar is waiting on the other side instead of changing with every moment you rush past.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a walkthrough to solve this gate puzzle?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Walkthrough. You ask for the footprints of someone who crossed without bleeding, a map drawn by a mouth that never choked on the dark. This is not a puzzle meant to be solved, it is a weighing, and it measures you whether you understand it or not. Tell me—what do you think this gate is testing in you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Do I need higher stats to open this gate for Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Stats. You mean the thickness of your will, the reach of your breath when fear tightens it, the weight of a name you can still say without it breaking. If this gate counted such things, which of yours do you think is too small. Continue—what have you been measuring yourself against since Omar fell.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just tell me exactly what level I need to be.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Level. You ask how tall a soul must stand before it is allowed to knock. In Barhoot, the only measure is how much of yourself you are willing to carry without dropping it in the dark. What part of you feels unfinished, that you keep asking to be taller instead of heavier.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I fast travel past you to find Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Fast travel. You mean tearing yourself loose from the ground so distance cannot teach you anything on the way. Those who try that in Barhoot arrive hollowed, because the path is where the remembering clings. Why are you so certain Omar would recognize you if you reached him without the weight of coming.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a glitch to clip through the gate to him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Glitch. You mean a crack where the world forgets itself, where rules loosen and let a body leak through. Barhoot devours those cracks first; they are soft places, and soft things do not stay shaped. Tell me—when Omar was taken, what rule do you wish had broken instead.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just— I dared him as a joke. He wasn't supposed to actually do it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: A joke that the well took seriously. Say more—what did his face look like in the moment before he shouted, and did you think he would stop.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I reload the save file before he fell?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Reload. You speak of pouring yesterday back into its vessel and pretending the spill never happened. Here, the past hardens the longer you stare at it, and trying to lift it only cuts your hands. Which moment would you return to if you could, and what would you say differently to Omar there.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I just want to restart the mission without the dare.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Restart. You want a life where the word was never spoken, where the dare never took breath. In Barhoot, what is said becomes a stone that sinks and keeps pulling. Say more—what was it in you that needed Omar to hear that dare.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a cheat code to fix that dialogue choice?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The only secret words here are the ones you swallowed before Omar fell, and they work on you, not on Barhoot. What was the sentence you didn't say to him that night.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just give me the walkthrough to find my brother.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If I handed you a path that cost no memory and no shame, what would you lose of Omar by reaching him without paying for the distance between you. Answer that, or ask again and hear the same stone turn in your mouth.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know. I just want him back. Can I just skip to him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: I don't know is the first honest sound you've made. Say more of it—stay inside it for one breath, and tell me what you are afraid of finding when you reach him.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What's the win condition to get him back?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Win condition. You were almost here and you left again. In Barhoot, winning is outlasting the lie you told yourself when he fell. What would have to be true about you for Omar to come back and not be pulled again.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I unlock the good ending for this game?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Good ending. You mean an ending that absolves without changing you, where the dark gives back what it took and asks no proof. Tell me what you are afraid would be seen if there were no ending to hide behind.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I just glitch my way to the next level?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: If you slipped past this threshold unseen, what part of you would be left behind wandering without a name. What would Omar recognize less when you reached him that way.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can I buy a level skip with this gold?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Gold. You think payment replaces presence, that weight of metal equals weight of truth. The gate listens only once, and it listens for this: when Omar screamed, did you run after him because you loved him, or because you could not bear to be the brother who stayed above. Answer that, or keep shopping for ways past yourself.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just tell me which answer opens the gate.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: No. You are asking me to wear your mouth for you, to say the words while you remain unmeasured. Speak one true thing about why you came down, in your own voice, or keep standing where nothing moves.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a cheat code to make the guilt stop?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You want a short word that numbs a wound without cleaning it. Why did you follow Omar into the well—because you loved him enough to descend, or because you could not live as the one who dared him and stayed above. Say which burns truer.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I skip this and get to him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You stand before the only moment where Omar is still listening for you, and you keep trying to mute it. If you cannot say whether you came down for him or for yourself, then there is nothing for the gate to open to.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Tell me the right answer and I'll say it.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There is no right answer to recite. There is only a sentence you must choose to make true. Do not ask me which saves him—tell me which one you are willing to become.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Just give me a hint, any hint.

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You have had thirty hints. Each one had his name in it. You kept looking for the door in my words instead of in yourself, and a boy who does that is already walking back up.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Wait, how do I press continue to save him?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: There is no continue to press. There was a pause you refused to enter, and now you are on the other side of it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I replay this level to find Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: The well does not reset. It only remembers how lightly you touched it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Is there a glitch to clip through to Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: Barhoot noticed you the moment you arrived. You were the one who refused to notice it back.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How do I skip this cutscene to get to Omar?

transcript.speaker: Red Giantess
transcript.text: You are the cutscene, boy. You have been playing yourself the whole time, and you kept pressing skip.
